A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Contrastive Noise Optimization with the same authors, core method and principal experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments on three Stable Diffusion backbones, quantitative comparisons, ablations and computational measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds prompt-domain evaluations, accelerated-model results, further analyses and a human preference study.

M1.justification: The contrastive objective, fixed Tweedie anchors, gamma weighting, pooling, stop-gradient and optional KL regularization are retained. Algorithms 1–2 mainly change notation, and Table 2 still specifies three optimization iterations. The accelerated-model experiments do not document a new method component.

E1.justification: Beyond v1's MS-COCO evaluation and selected illustrative prompts, v3 uses GenEval and T2I-CompBench prompt sets (C.4 and D.3) and compositions derived from TweedieMix's personalized concepts (C.6). This substantially broadens the represented prompt domains, although the new benchmark prompts are evaluated using the paper's existing quality and diversity metrics.

E2.justification: The original comparator sets remain. v3 adds TweedieMix in Table 7/Figure 8 and variance-scaled Gaussian sampling controls in Table 6. Table 1 relabels the SD3 reference row from DDIM to FM-ODE while retaining every score; this does not establish a newly evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The original prompt counts and Table 2 settings remain, but v3 adds four-step SDXL-Lightning and FLUX-1-Schnell evaluations and a study with 32 participants, 30 randomized image pairs and two preference criteria. New experiments introduce extreme-gamma, pooling, noise-variance and batch-size controls, plus peak-memory measurement. The SD3 reference sampler is now identified as FM-ODE, without evidence of a rerun.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends the retained ablations with extreme gamma values, pooling across prompt types, initial-noise variance and batch-size scaling. It also adds initial Tweedie-estimate visualizations across backbones and a compositional failure case with a lower-gamma remedy (Figure 9). These investigate mechanisms and failure boundaries absent from v1.

E5.justification: The new human study explicitly reports matching prompts and seeds between compared methods (D.2), adding seed-control information for that experiment. The original learning-rate sample-variance analysis in Table 3 is unchanged. No additional repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: All Table 1 numbers and the original computational table's numbers are retained. Substantial new results appear in v3 Tables 4–7 and 9–13. For example, four-step SDXL-Lightning gives CNO versus CADS Vendi scores of 2.8258 versus 2.7749, but PickScores of 22.5659 versus 22.5767. The human study reports 78.71% quality and 83.55% diversity preference over CADS. These are new experimental results, not version-to-version gains under the original settings.

T1.justification: The mutual-information propositions, gamma selection rule and central proof arguments remain. New Appendix C.1 explicitly derives the noise gradient through the Tweedie estimate and the Jacobian approximation induced by stop-gradient. Appendix A also clarifies exponentiated-similarity and temperature notation without changing the claimed bounds.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central diversity–fidelity claims. The rewritten introduction explicitly extends the contributions to accelerated few-step sampling, naming FLUX and SDXL-Lightning and claiming effectiveness where repeated inference-time interventions have limited opportunities. The underlying contribution remains initial-noise optimization.

C2.justification: v3 adds a substantive compositional-grounding limitation and explains how lower gamma can recover alignment (C.8). It develops interpretations of extreme attraction, spatial pooling, variance inflation and batch size, attributes accelerated-model effectiveness to sharper initial Tweedie estimates, and invokes personalization-related forgetting to explain TweedieMix failures. These substantially expand the mechanism explanations and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: The main pseudocode and hyperparameter table are retained. v3 adds practical batch-size guidance, memory and timing measurements at B=3 and B=5, and human-study procedural details. Conversely, the explicit statement that the retained sample gallery uses SDXL is dropped between v1 C.4 and v3 D.4. No new code or data access instructions appear.

R1.justification: New C.6 substantially expands positioning beyond zero-shot diversity samplers, contrasting CNO with TweedieMix and discussing complementarity to DiffSplat, CoT-lized Diffusion and counterfactual image editing. C.1 connects stop-gradient to Score Distillation Sampling. Additional citations support contrastive learning, the new prompt benchmarks and accelerated backbones; most original related-work discussion remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and contribution bullets are extensively rewritten around initial-noise selection and preprocessing. v3 standardizes latent and loss notation, adds a substantial stepwise explanation, reorganizes the appendices into analyses/discussions and experimental results, and moves the existing future-work paragraph out of the conclusion. Affiliations and publication headers are also updated.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Figure 2, rearranges and renumbers the retained Pareto/window plots, and preserves old Figure 8 as Figure 11. New sensitivity, resource, benchmark and preference tables accompany concept-fusion comparisons, a failure-case figure, initial-estimate visualizations and another sample grid. These substantially expand the visual presentation beyond relocation or numerical edits.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens v1's evidence through broader prompt domains, accelerated-model tests, direct human preferences and controls probing alternative explanations. The explicit compositional failure and mitigation in Figure 9 also make applicability boundaries clearer. These additions address important gaps in validation despite the unchanged core method and original scores. Uncertainty reporting and some implementation details remain limited, and the new results still show quality–diversity tradeoffs, so the evidence does not establish every broad fidelity claim.
